claim.quote: We have measured the parity-violating electroweak asymmetry in the elastic scattering of polarized electrons from the proton.

name: HAPPEX-I: parity-violating asymmetry in elastic electron-proton scattering at Q^2 = 0.477 (GeV/c)^2

summary.plain: A new HAPPEX measurement of the tiny difference in how spin-polarised electrons scatter from protons, made with an electron source and a Compton polarimeter that were firsts for such an experiment. It left room for only a small strange-quark contribution.
summary.technical: A = -15.05 +- 0.98 stat +- 0.56 syst ppm at <theta_lab> = 12.3 degrees and Q^2 = 0.477 (GeV/c)^2, giving G_E^s + 0.392 G_M^s = 0.025 +- 0.020 +- 0.014; first fixed-target parity-violation experiment to use a strained GaAs photocathode or a Compton polarimeter.

title: New Measurement of Parity Violation in Elastic Electron-Proton Scattering and Implications for Strange Form Factors
why_it_matters: Showed that the parity-violation technique reaches the precision needed to test for strange-quark effects in the proton.
